text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities — A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 — each ran in about half of the traces in the earlier window (roughly 97–103 of 200 traces each) but in nearly all traces in the later window (197–199 of 200), moving from optional to near-mandatory. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]
- In the earlier window the two groups {A33, A35, A36} and {A37, A38, A39} were mutually exclusive alternatives: cross-group pairs never co-occurred (0 of 200 traces), while activities within a group always ran together. In the later window, cross-group pairs co-occur in about 196–197 of 200 traces, with the A33/A35/A36 group placed before the A37/A38/A39 group in about 97 in 100 of those traces; order within each group remains mixed (both orders in similar shares) in both windows. [REL039, REL041, REL046, REL048, REL037, REL042, REL049, REL051]
- The blocks also became firmly anchored between their neighbours: A30 now precedes the A33/A35/A36 group in about 98 in 100 traces (earlier the group ran without A30 in about half), A31 now follows it in about 98 in 100 (earlier A31 ran without the group in about half), and the group now co-occurs with A14, A15 and A16 in nearly every trace (about 49–52 in 100 earlier), following A14 almost always. [REL025, REL031, REL007, REL013, REL019]
- Routing and distances changed accordingly: A30's outgoing transitions now go almost only to A35, A33 and A36 (about 37%, 30% and 30%), and A33/A35/A36 now lead to A37/A38/A39 (about 8–12% each) instead of to A31, whose share fell from about 30–36% to under 1%; gaps from A30 to A37–A39 and from A33/A35/A36 to A31 grew from 1–3 steps earlier to 4–5 steps in the later window. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG003, LAG006]
- A04 became rarer and rerouted: it appears in about 27 of 200 later traces versus about 61 earlier; the share of its outgoing transitions going to A16 fell from about 81% to about 36%, with new successors such as A15 (about 18%) and A48 (about 14%), and the direct A04→A16 adjacency fell from about 98% to about 59% of co-occurring traces (only 15 co-occurrences in the later window, so this part rests on few observations). [OCC001, DIR002, LAG001, POS001]
- A06 and A10, seen in about 6 and 5 of 200 earlier traces, appear in about 22 and 24 later traces — roughly tripled, but still rare. [OCC002, OCC003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two previously alternative branches became two sequential, near-mandatory stages: the group A33/A35/A36 and the group A37/A38/A39, which in the earlier window each ran in about half of the traces and never together, now both run in almost every trace, with A33/A35/A36 consistently before A37/A38/A39 (about 97 in 100), and A31 now following the combined block (about 98 in 100) instead of running without the first group in half the traces. [OCC004, OCC009, REL039, REL046, REL048, REL031, REL033]

This hypothesis is direct and consistent: the relational items show the alternatives-together change itself, the participation items show both groups moving from about 49–52 to about 99 in 100 traces, the routing items show A30 feeding the first group and the first group feeding the second rather than A31, and the lag items shift by roughly the length of the second group. The screening produced 89 qualifying control-flow items against about 1 expected if nothing had changed, so the ensemble is far beyond what an unchanged process typically yields; note, however, that many items describe overlapping aspects of the same trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations. The evidence cannot rule out that the earlier window mixed process variants or that the change was gradual across the boundary, since only two aggregate windows of 200 traces are compared, and the residual 1–2 in 100 traces without the blocks cannot be interpreted. [REL039, OCC004, DIR006, LAG006]

Other differences: A04's participation halved (about 61 → 27 of 200 traces) and its outgoing routing redistributed away from A16 (about 81% → 36% of its outgoing transitions, with new successors and a loosened A04→A16 adjacency), and A06 and A10 roughly tripled in participation while remaining rare (about 3% → 11% and 2.5% → 12% of traces); these changes are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC001, DIR002, LAG001, OCC002, OCC003]
